_comment: A ratchet on the iOS accessibility audit's exemptions (LabImporterUITests/AccessibilityAuditUITests.swift). 'unmeasured' lists, as what it covers (condition, audit type, element as its full label, null for an issue without an element and "" for any; limit absent for none), every entry of AuditExemption.entries the audit lets go without measuring it: hit regions, clipped text, element detection, and contrast without a named element (null, an issue without one, or "", whichever element the audit points at). 'rules' counts the exemptions AuditExemption.reason grants by rule before any entry; the audit counts each rule it applies as unmeasured. A contrast entry naming its element by its full label isn't listed: the audit lets it go only while that element's own pixels measure 4.5:1 on that run (it counts and prints what it measured, and fails one it couldn't), so such entries may be added or changed freely. static_metrics.py --gate fails when the audit's unmeasured entries differ from this list (one added, widened or narrowed, or gone without being removed here) or it has more rules, and CI fails a pull request whose list lets go anything the base branch's didn't. It may only go down: an entry for an issue without an element may give way to one naming the element by its full label, on the same or a narrower page with the same or a lower limit.
_pages: 'pages' lists each screen of QualityScreen.all (LabImporterUITests/QualityScreens.swift) with how many pages at the largest text the pull-request audit looks at (auditedPages) and, as laterPages, whether it leaves the pages after them alone (the weekly run of quality.yml audits every page, QUALITY_AUDIT_ALL_PAGES=1). static_metrics.py --gate fails when a screen audits other pages than listed, and CI fails a pull request whose list has a screen gone, fewer pages, or later pages newly left alone compared with the base branch's: pages may only go up.
